claims.text: Heating boride-based components in air at about 900°C for 1–2 hours will develop a continuous oxide scale.
The pre-oxidation treatment will form a coherent, adherent oxide scale.
The oxide scale will likely comprise boron oxides and minor metal oxides.
The pre-formed oxide scale will act as a diffusion barrier.
The oxide layer will impede direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying boride material.
Impeding direct contact will reduce interfacial reactions between molten aluminum and the boride material.
The oxide layer will slow aluminum penetration into the boride material.
Pre-oxidation will improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components.
Pre-oxidized specimens will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than untreated specimens during exposure to molten aluminum.
Pre-oxidized specimens will show lower weight loss than untreated specimens.
Pre-oxidized specimens will show less interfacial degradation than untreated specimens.
Untreated boride-based components typically have higher corrosion rates because molten aluminum directly attacks their surfaces.
The corrosion benefit depends on the oxide scale remaining thermodynamically stable during molten-aluminum exposure.
The corrosion benefit depends on the oxide scale remaining mechanically adherent during molten-aluminum exposure.
Mechanical disruption or thermal degradation of the oxide scale may eliminate the corrosion-resistance benefit.
